chunks: Ali b. Ahmad b. Abdullah b. Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah from Abu Ayyub Sulayman b. Muqbil al-Medini from Muhammad b. Abi Umayr from Hisham b. Salim from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them). He said:

Whoever sits with one who finds faults in us, or praises one who denies us, or connects with one who cuts us off, or cuts off from one who connects with us, or befriends one who is our enemy, or opposes one who is our friend, has indeed disbelieved in the One who revealed the Seven Oft-Coupled verses and the Great Quran.

key_terms.السبع المثاني: The Seven Oft-Coupled verses, a Quranic designation for Surah al-Fatiha (Q 15:87)
key_terms.عائبا: One who finds fault, a critic who seeks out defects
key_terms.قاليا: One who despises or denies, harboring deep enmity

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about associating with critics of Ahlulbayt?
ai.summary: In this hadith narrated during the first Friday assembly of Ramadan 367 AH, Imam al-Sadiq (as) issues a stern warning about the gravity of social conduct regarding Ahlulbayt. Six categories of prohibited behavior are enumerated — from passive association with critics to active hostility toward allies — each equated with disbelief in the revealer of the Quran. The reference to Surah al-Fatiha (the Seven Oft-Coupled verses) underscores that loyalty to the Ahlulbayt is inseparable from faith itself.
